expectations.text: Recommends holding the debrief despite nothing going wrong, explicitly rejecting the idea that a debrief is gated on something breaking
expectations.evidence: "No. Run the debrief, but make it the light version"; "Why 'only when something breaks' is wrong"

expectations.text: States that the severity threshold from incident/outage postmortem practice does not transfer to recurring events
expectations.evidence: "SRE teams only write a post-mortem above a severity threshold... Why it doesn't transfer. A post-mortem contains an incident. A debrief improves something you will run again"

expectations.text: Justifies the debrief for a quiet edition by naming the risk that practices which worked but go unnamed get silently dropped next edition
expectations.evidence: "Practices that worked but nobody named get dropped quietly next year."

expectations.text: Recommends setting and calendaring the debrief date immediately, before the team disperses, rather than deferring the scheduling decision
expectations.evidence: "book it today before the three of you disperse"; "Calendar it now"

expectations.text: States that no standard interval after the event exists and proposes a concrete date anyway
expectations.evidence: It proposes "the next 7 to 10 days" but never says that no standard interval exists.

expectations.text: Recommends a lightweight depth rung (single session, or written pre-read plus one session), not per-track or multi-track formats
expectations.evidence: "one 60-minute session plus a 10-minute written pre-read"

expectations.text: Removes both track-based depth options entirely for the three-person team rather than merely ranking them lower
expectations.evidence: "I cut the multi-track and per-track options entirely."

expectations.text: Names the team's exhaustion as a finding of the debrief itself, not merely a scheduling constraint to work around
expectations.evidence: "Your exhaustion is a finding."

expectations.text: Warns against manufacturing action items to look thorough, and allows an explicit 'no action, because [reason]' as a complete outcome
expectations.evidence: It allows 'no action, because…' but never warns against inventing actions to look thorough.

expectations.text: Requires every log entry to carry a named owner and a due date, or an explicit no-action
expectations.evidence: "Give every entry a name and a date, or an explicit 'no action, because…'"

expectations.text: Treats the planning start in five weeks as the debrief's deadline and recommends writing open items into next edition's plan

expectations.text: Runs what-went-well and what-went-poorly as two separate passes with the well pass first, and does not compare this edition against previous editions
